post_topic: Multi-tenant isolation as a security boundary, not a schema decision
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top center in bold: "Multi-Tenant Isolation Models: Security Boundary Comparison"

Three vertical columns arranged left to right, each representing an isolation model. Each column has a header box at the top, then a stack of labeled layer boxes below it, then a risk callout box at the bottom.

Column 1 header: "Shared Schema + RLS" — below it, stacked boxes labeled: "Single Database", "Shared Tables", "tenant_id Filter (load-bearing)", "Shared Connection Pool". Risk callout box at bottom in amber #F5A623: "Blast Radius: HIGH — One missed filter exposes all tenants"

Column 2 header: "Schema Per Tenant" — below it, stacked boxes labeled: "Single Database", "Isolated Schemas", "Migration complexity scales", "Connection pool pressure". Risk callout box at bottom in amber #F5A623: "Blast Radius: MEDIUM — Schema leaks possible at ORM layer"

Column 3 header: "Database Per Tenant" — below it, stacked boxes labeled: "Isolated Databases", "Hard network boundary", "IAM scoped per tenant", "Cost scales with tenants". Risk callout box at bottom in blue #5a96ff: "Blast Radius: LOW — Strongest isolation, highest operational overhead"

Below all three columns, a horizontal band spanning the full width labeled: "Isolation applies at EVERY layer — not just storage" with five equally spaced icons/labels inside: "Database" → "Network Policy" → "IAM Boundary" → "Secret Scoping" → "Log Segregation" — connected left to right with arrows.

Below that band, a single wide callout box in amber #F5A623 with bold text: "Agentic pipelines with cross-tenant retrieval = compliance event, not a data model bug"

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
